title: bug: services-http read fails when the response has no Content-Length (regression in 0.59)
body:
### OpenDAL version or commit

0.59.4 (0.59.0 and later). The same code works with 0.58.2.

### Affected service or component

`services-http` (read and stat), via `raw::http_util::parse_into_metadata` in `opendal-core`.

### Describe the bug

Since 0.59, reading a file through the HTTP service fails whenever the server's response has no `Content-Length` header:

```
Unexpected (permanent) at read, context: { service: http, path: file.txt, range: 0- } => HTTP response does not contain file content length
```

`Content-Length` is optional in HTTP. HTTP/1.1 responses can be framed with `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` (RFC 9112 §6), and in HTTP/2 the end of the stream marks the end of the body (RFC 9113 §8.1.1). RFC 9110 §8.6 only says a server *should* send it when the size is known in advance.

The check appears to come from #8196, which made `parse_into_metadata` require a content length for files. `services-http` calls it on every read (`reader.rs`) and every stat (`backend.rs`), and there is no option to turn the requirement off. In 0.58.2 the length was optional and the same read succeeds.

This affects real deployments. Cloudflare serves responses it does not cache (`cf-cache-status: BYPASS`) without `Content-Length`: chunked over HTTP/1.1 and with no length over HTTP/2, for both GET and HEAD. Cached responses do carry the header. For example, `https://history.stellar.org/prd/core-live/core_live_001/.well-known/stellar-history.json`, a Stellar history archive file read through the HTTP service, can no longer be read with 0.59.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Run a server that answers with a chunked response (`server.py`):

```python
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer

class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    protocol_version = "HTTP/1.1"

    def do_GET(self):
        body = b"hello world\n"
        self.send_response(200)
        self.send_header("Transfer-Encoding", "chunked")
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(b"%x\r\n%s\r\n0\r\n\r\n" % (len(body), body))

HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 18080), Handler).serve_forever()
```

2. Read from it with the HTTP service (`Cargo.toml` has `opendal = { version = "=0.59.4", features = ["services-http"] }` and `tokio` with `macros` and `rt-multi-thread`):

```rust
use opendal::{services::Http, Operator};

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() {
    let op = Operator::new(Http::default().endpoint("http://127.0.0.1:18080")).unwrap();
    match op.read("file.txt").await {
        Ok(buf) => println!("ok: read {} bytes", buf.len()),
        Err(e) => println!("error: {e}"),
    }
}
```

### Actual Behavior

With 0.59.4:

```
error: Unexpected (permanent) at read, context: { service: http, path: file.txt, range: 0- } => HTTP response does not contain file content length
```

### Expected Behavior

The read succeeds, as it does with 0.58.2 and the same code:

```
ok: read 12 bytes
```

The content length in read and stat metadata should stay optional when the server does not send it.

### Additional Context

Until this changes, applications reading from servers or CDNs that stream responses have to stay on 0.58.x.

### Reproduction confirmation

- [x] I reproduced this issue against the affected component, both with the local server above and against `history.stellar.org` behind Cloudflare.

# Rationale for this change

<!--
Why are you proposing this change? If this is already explained clearly in the issue then this section is not needed.
Explaining clearly why changes are proposed helps reviewers understand your changes and offer better suggestions for fixes.
-->

OpenDAL uses `Service` for its internal storage abstraction, but module names and contributor guidance still refer to the former accessor architecture. Align these references with the current implementation.

# What changes are included in this PR?

<!--
There is no need to duplicate the description in the issue here but it is sometimes worth providing a summary of the individual changes in this PR.
-->

- Rename `raw/accessor.rs` to `raw/service.rs`, preserving existing raw type exports.
- Rename the implementation guide from `internals::accessor` to `internals::service`, update its link, and document the `Composer` associated type.
- Update `Operation` documentation to reference `Service`.
- Update `AGENTS.md` to describe current service boundaries, layer hooks, operation contexts, and operation body types.

title: ci(moonbit): update pinned MoonBit version

labels.description: This PR changes 0-9 lines, ignoring generated files.

body:
# Which issue does this PR close?

N/A, I notice current MoonBit URL seems to be broken
Unrelated PR: https://github.com/apache/opendal/pull/8381
Failed CI pipeline https://github.com/apache/opendal/actions/runs/37308702860/job/111758538166?pr=8381

# Rationale for this change

I checked latest release v0.14
```sh
hjiang@hjiangs-MacBook-Pro$ curl -sSIL \
  '[https://cli.moonbitlang.com/binaries/0.10.14%2B7d59c7ec9/moonbit-linux-x86_64.tar.gz](https://cli.moonbitlang.com/binaries/0.10.14%2B7d59c7ec9/moonbit-linux-x86_64.tar.gz)'
HTTP/2 200 
content-type: application/x-tar
content-length: 94206941
last-modified: Sun, 20 Sep 2026 09:43:55 GMT
x-amz-expiration: expiry-date="Fri, 20 Nov 2026 00:00:00 GMT", rule-id="delete binaries every 60days"
x-amz-server-side-encryption: AES256
accept-ranges: bytes
server: AmazonS3
date: Sun, 04 Oct 2026 16:32:33 GMT
etag: "b514d4133cfb9cec94d2d8e79d2b47b1-12"
x-cache: Hit from cloudfront
via: 1.1 663bb84d90dc678d22cfa3b5a0fbd7ac.cloudfront.net (CloudFront)
x-amz-cf-pop: SFO53-P8
x-amz-cf-id: yD_uS6shSsMiofM3wOOcBwjJU3483ny6PtriEB0Djo46NoK8cxwEUQ==
age: 73406
```
Notice the expiration
> x-amz-expiration: expiry-date="Fri, 20 Nov 2026 00:00:00 GMT", rule-id="delete binaries every 60days"

MoonBit’s S3 bucket applies a lifecycle rule that deletes versioned binary and core artifacts after 60 days. This means any CI workflow pinned to a specific MoonBit version will eventually fail once that artifact expires.

Alternative considered: using latest makes CI non-reproducible.

# What changes are included in this PR?

Update pinned MoonBit version from 0.10.6 to 0.10.14

# Are there any user-facing changes?

No

# Breaking changes

# AI Usage Statement

GPT-5.6
